learning_outcomes.text: Students deepen their theoretical knowledge on modelling, machine design, tolerancing, material choosing.

Students can apply the content of the theoretical part of this course, together with the whole experience acquired in basic Drawing, Machine Design, Applied Mechanics and Technology to practical applications in the mechanical and industrial fields.
Students will disassemble, study, re-design and model actual machine assemblies and components.
Modelling is performed by utilizing advanced design-and-drawing CAD 3D tools.

syllabus_topics: Choice of the right shape, dimensioning and tolerancing of components performed by fusion, forging, stamping, rolling, shearing, punching, drawing and deep drawing
Choice of dimensional tolerances in hub-shaft interference fit
Functional analysis and identification of the tolerancing chains in actual mechanical assemblies
Form, Orientation, Location and Run-out geometrical tolerancing
Teamwork in classroom (measuring and sketching existing industrial components and assemblies, performing improvements, shape optimization, dimensioning, tolerancing, material selection, etc.)

Individual activity (making models for components and assemblies through 3D CAD modeller, carrying out constructive 2D drawings from 3D models; optimization or re-design of some peculiar aspects of components or assemblies)
teaching_methods: Physical disassemblage of mechanical assemblies and hand sketching of components in working groups
3D modelling and 2D layout of assemblies and mechanical components individually under supervision

assessment_methods.method: CAD laboratory further test (if lack in frequency)

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. Admission to the oral test is conditioned upon achieving a minimum score of 18/30 in the written test. Positive results to the written test are valid until the winter session of the next solar year. If there is a lack of frequency in the CAD laboratory, a further test using a solid modeler is required before the oral exam. The global score depends on oral test answers, the value of laboratory drawings, copybook contents, the survey made in the first step of the oral test, and the written test score.
